subject: A single mature Hericium erinaceus fruiting body growing out of a wound in the trunk of a standing beech, roughly chest height, the white cushion of spines hanging clear of the bark. Woodland floor and further trunks falling away out of focus behind it.

Macro study of the underside of a fresh lion's mane, filling the frame with the hanging white spines. Held close enough that individual spines separate and taper to points, with the denser flesh they grow from just readable at the top of the frame.
A torn wound in the trunk of a mature beech where a limb has broken away, the exposed heartwood weathered grey against smooth grey bark. No fungus present, just the site.
Four or five pieces of dried lion's mane fruiting body arranged loosely on stone, cream to tan, hard and fibrous, with the cut stubs of the spines visible along one edge of the largest piece.

A low heap of pale milled grain-grown mushroom material on stone, floury and off-white, with fragments of oat husk and unmilled kernel visible in it. A shallow furrow drawn through the heap to show the texture.
Whole oat groats spilled in a loose drift across dark slate, a few hundred grains, some standing proud of the pile so the shape of the individual kernel reads clearly.
A conical heap of fine tan spray-dried extract powder on stone, with two pieces of dried mushroom laid beside it for comparison of colour and texture. The powder undisturbed, its surface smooth.
